LESSON: BELIEF IN QADAR

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.2: Belief in Qadar

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Belief in Qadar. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should Muslims believe in Qadar and Qadha?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman
2. appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BELIEF IN QADAR
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Belief in Qadar helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BELIEF IN QADAR
Study Belief in Qadar like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Belief in Qadar” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Belief in Qadar in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Belief in Qadar is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Belief in Qadar” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Belief in Qadar in your own words. (skill: appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Belief in Qadar to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Belief in Qadar from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Belief in Qadar: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Belief in Qadar?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should Muslims believe in Qadar and Qadha?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Belief in Qadar means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman.
5. Be able to: appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
